I will keep my full 5.0 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that matches my land, my experience, and the water access I have from the well. I have farmed for 25 years, so I will not do anything too risky this year. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the fertilizer in a balanced way, irrigate a few key times, and keep rotary tillage because it saves labor and fits my small farm. For maize, I will also plant the full 5.0 mu after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed for stable production, apply enough nitrogen to support yield, and rely on fewer irrigations because summer rain can help, with the well as backup. Since some family members work off-farm, I will choose a management style that is steady, not too labor-heavy, and aimed at dependable grain output rather than maximum risk-taking.
